mainTopic: פינחס's war against מדין and his family line; the משנה and גמרא on who is sent home from war, especially the man who built a new house.
overview: The גמרא finishes a ברייתא about what went out to war, using the פסוק of the war against מדין as support. A ברייתא says פינחס went to that war to avenge his ancestor יוסף. The גמרא shows that פינחס came from both יוסף and יתרו, and supports this from the plural word 'בנות'. A new משנה then lists who goes home from the battlefield: a man with a new house, a new vineyard, or a betrothed wife. These men still help the army with food, water and roads. The משנה also lists men who look similar but are not sent home, and men in their first year who do not leave home at all. The גמרא explains which announcements the כהן makes and which the שוטרים make. It then shows from the פסוק that any building fit to live in counts, however the man got it. At the end of the amud the גמרא begins asking whether excluding a robber fits רבי יוסי הגלילי, and that question continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The war against מדין shows what goes out to battle
steps.stepSummary: The text finishes saying that the לוחות were resting in the ארון. It brings the פסוק about the war against מדין to show that the סנהדרין, the משוח מלחמה, the ארון and the שופרות all went out to battle.
steps.simpleTranslation: ...were resting in the ארון. And the פסוק says the same thing: 'משה sent them, a thousand per tribe, them and פינחס.' 'Them' means the סנהדרין. 'פינחס' means the משוח מלחמה. 'The holy vessels' means the ארון and the לוחות inside it. 'The trumpets' means the שופרות.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes an earlier statement about what was taken out to war. It brings a פסוק from the war against מדין to back it up.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each phrase in the פסוק is matched to something that went out to battle. 'Them' becomes the סנהדרין, פינחס becomes the משוח מלחמה, the holy vessels become the ארון with its לוחות, and the trumpets become שופרות. This makes the war against מדין a model for how the Jewish army went out.

keyTerms.meaning: The tablets of the Ten Commandments
And so the פסוק says (brings support from a verse)
The כהן anointed to lead the army spiritually in war

phrases.english: were resting in the Ark.
phrases.notes: This finishes a sentence from the previous page about what lay inside the ארון taken out to war.

phrases.english: And similarly it says:
"And Moses sent them,
phrases.notes: במדבר 31:6

phrases.english: a thousand for each tribe, to the army,
them and Pinchas."
"Them": these are the Sanhedrin,
"Pinchas": this is the priest anointed for war,
"And the holy vessels": this is the Ark and the tablets inside it,
phrases.notes: These words come from later in the same פסוק.

phrases.english: "And the trumpets for the alarm": these are the shofars.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא from the previous page about the ארון going out to war.
steps.raayaObject: That the סנהדרין, the משוח מלחמה, the ארון with the לוחות, and שופרות go out to war.

steps.title: Why פינחס went to the war
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that פינחס went to fight מדין to avenge his mother's father, יוסף, whom the מדיינים sold to Egypt.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: פינחס did not go to the war for no reason. He went to collect the debt owed to his mother's father, as it says: 'And the מדיינים sold him into Egypt.'
steps.whatsHappening: A ברייתא gives the reason that פינחס in particular went to war against מדין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The מדיינים sold יוסף to Egypt, so his descendant had a family score to settle with them. The ברייתא assumes that פינחס's mother's father was יוסף. The גמרא will question that assumption next.

keyTerms.meaning: To collect a debt or punishment

phrases.english: It was taught:
Not for nothing did Pinchas go to the war,
rather, to exact the judgment owed to his mother's father,
phrases.notes: The ברייתא means יוסף, as the next פסוק shows.

phrases.english: as it is stated: "And the Midianites sold him
into Egypt, etc."
phrases.notes: בראשית 37:36

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנָא: לֹא לְחִנָּם הָלַךְ פִּינְחָס לַמִּלְחָמָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the mention of פינחס in the פסוק and explains why he was sent.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: פינחס went to war to avenge his mother's father, יוסף, against the מדיינים who sold him.

steps.title: Was פינחס descended from יתרו instead?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the claim that פינחס came from יוסף. The פסוק says his mother came from פוטיאל, and that name seems to point to יתרו, who fattened calves for idol worship.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does this mean פינחס came from יוסף? But it is written: 'אלעזר son of אהרן took for himself a wife from the daughters of פוטיאל.' Doesn't that mean he came from יתרו, who fattened calves for idol worship?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the ברייתא's claim about who פינחס's grandfather was.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The name פוטיאל is read as a play on 'פיטם', fattening animals. That points to יתרו, who once served idols. If פוטיאל is יתרו, then פינחס's mother's father was not יוסף.

keyTerms.meaning: Is this to say...? (starts a challenge)
The name of פינחס's maternal grandfather in the פסוק

phrases.english: Is this to say that Pinchas comes from Yosef?
But it is written:
"And Elazar son of Aharon took for himself
from the daughters of Putiel as a wife."
phrases.notes: שמות 6:25

phrases.english: Is it not that he comes from Yisro,
who fattened calves for idol worship?
phrases.notes: A play on the name: פוטיאל sounds like פיטם, 'fattened'.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְמֵימְרָא דְּפִינְחָס מִיּוֹסֵף אָתֵי? וְהָא כְּתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ברייתא in step 2.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's claim that פינחס's mother's father was יוסף.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק names the grandfather פוטיאל, which matches יתרו (פיטם עגלים), not יוסף.

steps.title: פוטיאל can refer to יוסף
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that פוטיאל can also point to יוסף, who 'פיטפט' (overpowered) his desire.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, he comes from יוסף, who mocked his desire.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends the ברייתא by reading the name פוטיאל another way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same name can be read as 'פיטפט', mocking or overpowering. That describes יוסף, who held back his desire. So the פסוק can still fit the ברייתא.

phrases.english: No, he comes from Yosef,
who mocked his desire.
phrases.notes: Another play on the name פוטיאל, this time pointing to יוסף's self-control.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 3.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: פוטיאל must mean יתרו, who fattened calves.
steps.terutzMaskana: פוטיאל can mean יוסף, who overpowered his desire.

steps.title: The tribes mocked פינחס for his idol-worshipping grandfather
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects using a tradition: the tribes mocked פינחס as the grandson of someone who fattened calves for idols. That shows his mother's father was יתרו.
steps.simpleTranslation: But didn't the tribes mock him, saying: 'Did you see this son of פוטי, whose mother's father fattened calves for idol worship? Will he kill a נשיא of ישראל?'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second challenge, showing that the people understood פינחס's maternal grandfather to be יתרו.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The tribes said 'his mother's father' fattened calves for idols. That is the exact relative the ברייתא said was יוסף. So the answer in step 4 seems to fall apart.

phrases.english: But weren't the tribes mocking him:
Did you see this son of Puti,
the son whose mother's father fattened
calves for idol worship,
and he should kill a prince of Israel!
phrases.notes: This is about פינחס killing זמרי, a tribal leader.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer of step 4.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that פוטיאל, his mother's father, was יוסף.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A tradition says his mother's father fattened calves for idols, which fits יתרו and not יוסף.

steps.title: פינחס descended from both יוסף and יתרו
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that פינחס's mother came from both families. One of her parents descended from יוסף and the other from יתרו.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather: if his mother's father came from יוסף, his mother's mother came from יתרו. And if his mother's mother came from יוסף, his mother's father came from יתרו.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא settles both challenges by giving פינחס two family lines.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is no need to choose between יוסף and יתרו. His mother's two parents came from the two families. So the ברייתא (from יוסף) and the tribes' mocking (from יתרו) are both true.
steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא does not decide which parent came from which family. It only says that one came from יוסף and the other from יתרו.

phrases.english: Rather:
if his mother's father was from Yosef,
his mother's mother was from Yisro,
and if his mother's mother was from Yosef,
his mother's father was from Yisro.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 5 and keeps the ברייתא of step 2.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: פינחס came from either יוסף or יתרו, but not both.
steps.terutzMaskana: פינחס came from both: one maternal grandparent from יוסף, the other from יתרו.

steps.title: The plural 'daughters' supports two family lines
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא supports its answer from the wording 'מבנות פוטיאל', which is plural and suggests two 'פוטיאל' families.
steps.simpleTranslation: The wording supports this too, since it is written 'from the daughters of פוטיאל', which suggests two. Learn from this.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that the פסוק's own wording hints at its answer, and it closes the discussion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'בנות' is plural, so it suggests that more than one family called פוטיאל stands behind פינחס's mother. That matches the answer that she came from both יוסף and יתרו.

keyTerms.meaning: Learn from it (the point is proven)

steps.whatToRemember: פינחס went to war against מדין to avenge יוסף. He came from both יוסף and יתרו, as the plural 'בנות פוטיאל' hints.

phrases.english: The wording is also precise,
as it is written: "from the daughters of Putiel,"
which implies two.
phrases.notes: 'בנות' is plural, so it hints at two families that each carry the name פוטיאל.

phrases.english: Learn from it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the answer of step 6 from the פסוק's wording.
steps.raayaObject: That פינחס came from two families.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: פינחס came from both יוסף and יתרו.

steps.title: The משנה: the man who built a new house
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה begins by quoting the פסוק where the שוטרים send home anyone who built a new house and has not yet dedicated it.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: 'And the officers shall speak to the people, saying: Who is the man who built a new house and has not dedicated it? Let him go and return to his house.'
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה opens by quoting the פסוק about the first group sent home from war. It sets up the details that come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before battle, the שוטרים announce who may leave. The first case is a man with a new house he has not yet started using. The משנה will now explain how wide this rule is.

keyTerms.meaning: Dedicated it, began living in it

phrases.english: Mishnah:
"And the officers shall speak to the people, saying:
phrases.notes: דברים 20:5

phrases.aramaic: מִי הָאִישׁ אֲשֶׁר בָּנָה בַיִת חָדָשׁ
phrases.english: Who is the man that built a new house
and has not dedicated it?
Let him go and return to his house, etc."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה about who goes home from the war camp.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A man who built a new house and has not dedicated it goes home from battle.

steps.title: Any kind of building counts
steps.stepSummary: The משנה says 'house' includes buildings no one lives in: a straw house, a cattle barn, a wood shed and a storehouse.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whether one builds a straw house, a cattle barn, a wood shed, or a storehouse.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה widens the word 'house' to cover many kinds of buildings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A beginner might think only a home to live in counts. The משנה says storage and farm buildings count too, so their builder also goes home.

phrases.english: Whether one builds a storehouse for straw,
a barn for cattle, a shed for wood,
or a warehouse.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the word 'בית' in the פסוק of step 8.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Any building counts, including those used for storage or animals.

steps.title: Any way of getting the house counts
steps.stepSummary: The משנה adds that the rule applies whether the man built, bought, inherited, or received the house as a gift.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whether one builds, or buys, or inherits, or is given it as a gift.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה widens the rule again, this time to how the man got the house.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says 'built', but the משנה includes every way of becoming the new owner. What matters is that he has a new house he has not yet used, not that he built it himself.
steps.whatToRemember: The new-house exemption covers every kind of building and every way of getting it: building, buying, inheriting, or receiving it as a gift.

phrases.english: Whether one builds, or one buys,
or one inherits,
or one to whom it was given as a gift.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Widens the rule from step 8 beyond the word 'בנה'.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Buying, inheriting, or receiving a house as a gift counts the same as building it.

steps.title: The man who planted a vineyard
steps.stepSummary: The משנה quotes the פסוק about a man who planted a כרם and says even five fruit trees count, even of five different kinds.
steps.simpleTranslation: "And what man has planted a vineyard and not yet used its fruit..." This applies to someone who planted a whole vineyard, and also to someone who planted only five fruit trees, even if they are five different kinds.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה moves to the next פסוק, about a man who planted a כרם, and defines how much planting counts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: You do not need a big vineyard to be sent home. Five fruit trees are enough. They do not even have to be the same kind of tree.

keyTerms.meaning: Made its fruit permitted for ordinary eating (after its first years), and so began to use it

phrases.english: "And what man is there who has planted a vineyard
and has not used its fruit, etc."
phrases.notes: דברים 20:6

phrases.english: Both one who plants a vineyard,
and one who plants five fruit trees,
and even from five different species.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Same pattern as the house in steps 8-10, now applied to the vineyard.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A vineyard or even five fruit trees, even of mixed kinds, exempts the man.

steps.title: Any way of planting or getting the vineyard counts
steps.stepSummary: Planting, layering or grafting all count, and so does buying, inheriting or receiving the vineyard as a gift.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whether he planted it, layered it, or grafted it, and whether he bought it, inherited it, or got it as a gift.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה widens the rule: it does not matter how the trees were planted or how the man came to own them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This matches what step 10 said about the house. What counts is that he has a new vineyard he has not yet enjoyed, not whether he planted it himself.

keyTerms.meaning: Layering: bending a branch into the ground so it roots as a new plant

phrases.english: Both one who plants, and one who layers,
phrases.notes: Layering means bending a vine branch into the ground so it takes root as a new vine.

phrases.english: and one who grafts,
and one who buys, and one who inherits,
and one to whom it was given as a gift.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Expands the vineyard case from step 11, just as step 10 expanded the house case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Every way of planting and every way of acquiring the vineyard counts.

steps.title: The man who is betrothed
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק about a betrothed man covers a virgin, a widow, and even a שומרת יבם, even if the brother died in this very war.
steps.simpleTranslation: "And what man has betrothed a woman..." This applies whether he betrothed a virgin or a widow. Even a woman waiting for him for יבום counts, and even if he heard that his brother died in this war, he goes back home.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה moves to the third פסוק, about a man who is betrothed, and defines which women count.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule is not limited to a first marriage to a virgin. A widow counts. Even a יבמה who is only waiting for him counts, though he has not betrothed her himself. This is true even if she only became his יבמה in the middle of this war.

keyTerms.meaning: A widow waiting for her late husband's brother to do יבום

phrases.english: "And what man is there who has betrothed a woman, etc."
phrases.notes: דברים 20:7

phrases.english: Both one who betroths a virgin,
and one who betroths a widow.
Even a woman waiting for her יבם,
phrases.notes: This is his own brother's widow, who is waiting for him to marry her through יבום.

phrases.english: and even if he heard that his brother died in the war —
he goes back home.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Third category in the list, after house and vineyard.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Any betrothal, and even a waiting יבמה, exempts the man.

steps.title: The exempt men still hear the speech and help the army
steps.stepSummary: All these men hear the כהן's speech at the camp, then go home, and they still supply water and food and fix the roads.
steps.simpleTranslation: All these men hear the words of the כהן about the rules of war, and then go back. They supply water and food and repair the roads.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה explains what happens to the men who are sent home: they first come to the camp, then leave, and they still help the war effort.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Being sent home does not mean they have nothing to do with the war. They must come and hear the speech before leaving. Afterward they still help by bringing supplies and fixing roads.

keyTerms.meaning: The rules and arrangements of war

phrases.english: All of these hear
the words of the כהן about the rules of war,
and they go back.
And they supply water and food,
and repair the roads.

steps.triggerLanguage: כׇּל אֵלּוּ וָאֵלּוּ שׁוֹמְעִין דִּבְרֵי כֹּהֵן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sums up the rule for every exempt man listed so far.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Exempt men come, hear the speech, return home, and still help with supplies and roads.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the contrast in step 20, where a different group does not even help with supplies.

steps.title: Men who are not sent home: minor buildings, too few trees, remarrying a divorcée
steps.stepSummary: A gatehouse, porch or balcony does not count as a house. Four fruit trees or five non-fruit trees do not count. Remarrying one's divorcée does not count.
steps.simpleTranslation: These are the men who do not go back: one who builds a gatehouse, a porch, or a balcony; one who plants four fruit trees or five non-fruit trees; one who remarries his divorced wife.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה now starts the opposite list: men who might look like they fit the פסוקים but are not sent home.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These cases fall short of each category. The buildings are not real houses, four trees are fewer than the minimum of five, and non-fruit trees are not like a vineyard. A man remarrying his own ex-wife is not taking a new wife.

keyTerms.meaning: Trees that do not bear fruit

steps.confusionAlert: Step 9 said even a straw house or barn counts as a house. So the line is not whether people actually live there. It is whether the building is fit to live in: a straw shed could be lived in, but a gatehouse, porch or balcony could not. The ברייתא in step 31 gives this reason.

phrases.english: And these are the ones who do not go back:
one who builds a gatehouse,
a porch, or a balcony;
one who plants four fruit trees
phrases.notes: Some versions add the letter in square brackets, so the word reads אַרְבָּעָה.

phrases.english: or five non-fruit trees;
one who takes back his divorced wife;

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from who is sent home to who is not.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Attachments to a house, fewer than five fruit trees, non-fruit trees, and remarrying one's divorcée do not exempt.

steps.title: A forbidden marriage does not send a man home
steps.stepSummary: A man betrothed to a woman the תורה forbids him to marry is not sent home.
steps.simpleTranslation: A widow betrothed to a כהן גדול; a divorcée or חלוצה to a regular כהן; a ממזרת or נתינה to a Jewish man; a Jewish woman to a ממזר or נתין. Such a man does not go back.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues the list of men who are not sent home and adds marriages that are forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The exemption is for a man looking forward to a marriage the תורה allows. If the marriage is forbidden, the תורה does not reward it by sending him home.

keyTerms.meaning: A widow released from יבום through חליצה
A woman born from a forbidden union

phrases.english: a widow to a High Priest,
a divorcée or a חלוצה to a regular כהן,
a ממזרת or a נתינה to a Jewish man,
a Jewish woman to a ממזר or a נתין —
he would not go back.
phrases.notes: This closes the whole list that began with 'these are the ones who do not go back' in step 15.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues and closes the list from step 15.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A betrothal the תורה forbids does not exempt from war.

steps.title: רבי יהודה and רבי אליעזר add more houses that do not count
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה says rebuilding a house as it was does not count. רבי אליעזר says building a brick house in the שרון does not count.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: even one who rebuilds a house on its old foundation does not go back. רבי אליעזר says: even one who builds a brick house in the שרון does not go back.
steps.whatsHappening: Two תנאים add more house cases to the list of men who are not sent home.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה holds that only a new house counts, not rebuilding one that stood there before. רבי אליעזר holds that a brick house in the שרון is not a lasting house, so it does not count either.

keyTerms.meaning: On its original place, as it stood before
The שרון, a region in ארץ ישראל

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: אַף הַבּוֹנֶה בַּיִת עַל מְכוֹנוֹ —
phrases.english: רבי יהודה says: even one who builds a house on its original foundation —
would not go back.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר: אַף הַבּוֹנֶה בֵּית לְבֵינִים בַּשָּׁרוֹן —
phrases.english: רבי אליעזר says: even one who builds a brick house in the Sharon —
phrases.notes: Brick houses there did not last and had to be rebuilt again and again.

phrases.english: would not go back.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: אַף הַבּוֹנֶה בַּיִת עַל מְכוֹנוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds cases to the 'do not go back' list from steps 15-16.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Per רבי יהודה a rebuilt house, and per רבי אליעזר a brick house in the שרון, do not exempt.

steps.title: Men who do not even leave their homes
steps.stepSummary: A man in the first year after dedicating his house, using his vineyard, marrying his ארוסה, or marrying his יבמה does not report to the army at all, based on a פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: These are the men who do not move from their place: one who built a house and dedicated it, planted a vineyard and began using it, married his betrothed, or married his יבמה. As it says: "He shall be free for his house one year."
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה opens a third group, men who are so fully exempt that they do not even come to the camp, and brings a פסוק as the source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first group had not yet finished: the house was not dedicated, the fruit not used, the woman only betrothed. This group has finished and is in the first year of enjoying it. The פסוק in דברים 24 gives such a man a full year at home.

keyTerms.meaning: Move from their place (do not even go to the camp)
One who marries his brother's widow through יבום

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix the two groups. Before finishing (not yet dedicated, used or married), he comes to the camp and then goes home. After finishing, during the first year, he does not come at all.

phrases.english: These are the ones who do not move from their place:
one who built a house and dedicated it,
planted a vineyard and used its fruit,
one who marries his betrothed,
one who marries his יבמה,
as it is said: "He shall be free for his house one year."
phrases.notes: דברים 24:5

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new, stronger group of exemptions.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In the first year after finishing house, vineyard or marriage, the man does not report at all.

steps.title: Reading each word of the פסוק to cover all four cases
steps.stepSummary: The משנה reads the words of the פסוק one by one: his house, his vineyard, his wife, and his יבמה.
steps.simpleTranslation: "For his house" — this is his house. "He shall be" — this is his vineyard. "And make his wife happy" — this is his wife. "Whom he has taken" — this comes to include his יבמה.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה shows how each of the four cases in step 18 comes from a different word in the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק is mainly about a new wife, but the משנה reads extra words to include the house and the vineyard. The words "whom he has taken" add the יבמה, whom the תורה gives to him rather than him choosing her by betrothal.
steps.whatToRemember: Three groups: (1) not yet finished — comes to camp, goes home, still helps; (2) does not qualify — fights; (3) first year after finishing — does not leave home at all.

phrases.english: "For his house" — this is his house,
"He shall be" — this is his vineyard,
"And he shall make his wife happy" — this is his wife,
"Whom he has taken" — to include his יבמה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how the פסוק quoted in step 18 covers each case.
steps.raayaObject: The four cases of step 18: house, vineyard, wife, יבמה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The words of דברים 24:5 read one by one.

steps.title: These men do not even help with supplies or roads
steps.stepSummary: Unlike the first group, men in their first year do not supply water and food or fix roads.
steps.simpleTranslation: They do not supply them with water and food, and they do not repair the roads.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה finishes this group by saying they are free even from the support jobs.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 14 said the first exempt group still helps with supplies and roads. This group is fully free for their year at home, so they do none of that.
steps.whyThisMatters: This completes the contrast with step 14 and shows how much stronger the 'first year' exemption is.

phrases.english: They do not supply them with water and food,
and they do not repair the roads.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the 'do not move from their place' group by contrast with step 14.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Men in their first year are free even from supplying the army and fixing roads.

steps.title: Do the officers say their own words?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks whether 'and the officers shall speak' means the שוטרים are saying their own words.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: 'And the officers shall speak.' Maybe this means they say their own words?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens with a ברייתא that raises a possible reading of the פסוק. This sets up the next move, which will show that the reading is wrong.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק (דברים כ:ה) says the שוטרים speak the 'new house' announcement. A simple reading would make these the officers' own words. The ברייתא raises this so it can test it.

keyTerms.meaning: The Rabbis taught; this opens a ברייתא
'One might think', a possible reading that is about to be tested

phrases.english: GEMARA: The Rabbis taught:
'And the officers shall speak'
phrases.notes: דברים 20:5

phrases.english: One might think: their own words?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא on the משנה's description of the war announcements.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Are the words in דברים כ:ה the officers' own words?

steps.title: A later פסוק proves these are the כהן's words
steps.stepSummary: The officers' own words are only introduced later with 'and the officers shall speak further', so the first speech belongs to the כהן משוח מלחמה.
steps.simpleTranslation: When the תורה later says 'and the officers shall speak further', that is where their own words are given. So what does the first 'and the officers shall speak' mean? The verse is talking about the words of the כהן anointed for war.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא proves the first speech belongs to the כהן. It points to a later פסוק where the officers speak for themselves.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'further' (ויספו) in דברים כ:ח marks the start of the officers' own speech. That means the earlier 'and the officers shall speak' cannot also be their own words. It must be the כהן משוח מלחמה's message, which they pass along.

keyTerms.meaning: The כהן anointed to lead the people in war

phrases.english: When it says 'and the officers shall speak further'
phrases.notes: דברים 20:8

phrases.english: there their own words are stated.
So how do I explain 'and the officers shall speak'?
The verse is speaking about the words of the priest anointed for war.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the possible reading raised in step 21.
steps.raayaObject: The first speech is the כהן's words, not the officers' own words.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The phrase 'ויספו השוטרים' in דברים כ:ח.

steps.title: The כהן speaks and the officer calls it out
steps.stepSummary: The two פסוקים fit together this way: the כהן says the words and the שוטר announces them loudly.
steps.simpleTranslation: How does this work? The priest speaks and the officer makes it heard.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא explains how both ideas can be true. The words belong to the כהן, but the שוטר is the one who announces them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This settles why the פסוק says 'the officers shall speak' about words that belong to the כהן. The officer is the loudspeaker who repeats the כהן's message to the army.

keyTerms.meaning: How so? How do these fit together?

steps.whatToRemember: The 'new house' speech is the כהן's message, announced out loud by a שוטר.

phrases.english: How so?
A priest speaks and an officer calls it out.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Wraps up the proof of step 22 into a working rule.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: In this section the כהן speaks and the שוטר announces.

steps.title: Three ברייתות disagree about who speaks
steps.stepSummary: One ברייתא says a כהן speaks and a שוטר announces. Another says a כהן speaks and a כהן announces. A third says a שוטר speaks and a שוטר announces.
steps.simpleTranslation: One ברייתא teaches: a priest speaks and an officer announces. Another teaches: a priest speaks and a priest announces. Another teaches: an officer speaks and an officer announces.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא lists three ברייתות that seem to contradict each other. This sets up אביי's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each ברייתא gives a different pair of speaker and announcer. If they all describe the same speech, they cannot all be right. That is the problem.

phrases.aramaic: תָּנֵי חֲדָא: כֹּהֵן מְדַבֵּר וְשׁוֹטֵר מַשְׁמִיעַ,
phrases.english: One teaches: a priest speaks and an officer announces;

phrases.aramaic: וְתַנְיָא אִידַּךְ: כֹּהֵן מְדַבֵּר וְכֹהֵן מַשְׁמִיעַ,
phrases.english: and another teaches: a priest speaks and a priest announces;

phrases.aramaic: וְתַנְיָא אִידַּךְ: שׁוֹטֵר מְדַבֵּר וְשׁוֹטֵר מַשְׁמִיעַ.
phrases.english: and another teaches: an officer speaks and an officer announces.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings sources that seem to clash with the rule of step 23.
steps.kashyaTarget: The single rule 'כהן מדבר ושוטר משמיע'.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Other ברייתות give different speaker and announcer pairs, so the sources contradict each other.

steps.title: אביי splits the speech into three sections
steps.stepSummary: אביי explains that each ברייתא describes a different section of the פסוקים.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: How does this work? From 'and he shall approach' until 'and they shall speak', a priest speaks and a priest announces. From 'and they shall speak' until 'and they shall speak further', a priest speaks and an officer announces. From 'and they shall speak further' and on, an officer speaks and an officer announces.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי resolves the contradiction. Each ברייתא is right about a different part of the announcements.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The opening encouragement belongs entirely to the כהנים. The list of men who go home (house, vineyard, wife) is the כהן's message announced by a שוטר. The section about the fearful man belongs entirely to the שוטרים.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And [the כהן] shall approach', the start of the speech

steps.whatToRemember: There are three sections: כהן and כהן, then כהן and שוטר, then שוטר and שוטר.

phrases.english: Abaye said: How so?
From 'and he shall approach' until 'and they shall speak'
phrases.notes: From דברים 20:2 until 20:5.

phrases.english: a priest speaks and a priest announces;
from 'and they shall speak' until 'and they shall speak further'
a priest speaks and an officer announces;
from 'and they shall speak further' and on
an officer speaks and an officer announces.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 24.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases: each source refers to a different section of the פסוקים.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: All three ברייתות describe the same speech and contradict each other.
steps.terutzMaskana: Each ברייתא describes a different section, so there is no contradiction.

steps.title: What about a house he bought, inherited, or received?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks how we know the exemption covers a house that was bought, inherited, or given as a gift, not only one he built.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'What man is there that built a new house...' The Rabbis taught: 'that built', I only know about one who built. From where do we know about one who bought, inherited, or was given it as a gift?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the משנה's 'new house' line and brings a ברייתא. The ברייתא asks whether getting a house in other ways also counts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'built' sounds limited to someone who built the house himself. The ברייתא asks for a source that includes other ways of getting a new house.

phrases.aramaic: ״מִי הָאִישׁ אֲשֶׁר בָּנָה בַיִת חָדָשׁ כּוּ׳״.
phrases.english: 'What man is there that built a new house, etc.'
phrases.notes: This quotes the משנה, which quotes דברים 20:5.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught: 'that built'
I only know about one who built.

phrases.aramaic: לָקַח וְיָרַשׁ וְנִיתַּן לוֹ בְּמַתָּנָה מִנַּיִן —
phrases.english: From where do we know about one who bought, inherited, or was given it as a gift?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: explaining the 'new house' line of the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source that includes a house he bought, inherited, or got as a gift.

steps.title: 'What man is there' includes all of them
steps.stepSummary: The fuller wording 'what man is there that built' includes any way of getting a house.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says: 'What man is there that built.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers from the extra words of the פסוק. Those words include the other cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה could have just said 'one who built'. The fuller phrase 'what man is there' widens the rule to include buying, inheriting, and receiving a house as a gift.

phrases.english: The verse says: 'What man is there that built.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 26.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The expanded phrase 'מי האיש אשר בנה' includes buying, inheriting, and gifts.

steps.title: What about storage buildings?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks how we know the exemption includes a straw shed, cattle barn, wood shed, or storehouse.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'A house': I only know about a house. From where do we include a straw shed, a cattle barn, a wood shed, and storehouses?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא now asks about the word 'house'. Do buildings that are not homes also count?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'house' sounds like only a home people live in. The ברייתא looks for a source that includes buildings used for storage or animals.

phrases.english: 'A house': I only know about a house.

phrases.aramaic: מִנַּיִן לְרַבּוֹת בֵּית הַתֶּבֶן, וּבֵית הַבָּקָר,
phrases.english: From where do we include a straw shed, a cattle barn,
a wood shed, and storehouses?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from how he got the house to what kind of building counts.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source that includes storage and animal buildings.

steps.title: 'That built' includes any building
steps.stepSummary: The words 'that built' include whatever he built.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says: 'that built', in any case.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers that 'that built' is broad. It covers any building.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא now reads 'that built' as covering whatever was built, not only a home. So storage buildings are included.

phrases.english: The verse says: 'that built', in any case.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 28.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'אשר בנה' includes any structure he built.

steps.title: Maybe even a gateway or balcony counts?
steps.stepSummary: If any building counts, maybe a gateway, an enclosed porch, or a balcony also counts.
steps.simpleTranslation: One might think I should include even one who builds a gateway, an enclosed porch, or a balcony.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא pushes the broad reading too far to test it. This sets up a limit in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If 'that built' covers everything, then even small add-ons like a gateway or balcony would count. The ברייתא raises this so it can limit the rule.

phrases.english: One might think I should include even one who builds
a gateway, an enclosed porch, or a balcony;

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests how far the broad reading of step 29 goes.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If every structure counts, then even gateways and balconies would count.

steps.title: Only a building fit for living counts
steps.stepSummary: The word 'house' limits the rule to buildings that are fit to live in.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says 'a house': just as a house is fit for living, so too anything fit for living.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא uses the word 'house' to set the limit. The building must be fit to live in.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A straw shed or a storehouse could be lived in, so it counts, even if he uses it for something else. A gateway, porch, or balcony is not fit for living, so it does not count.
steps.whatToRemember: The 'new house' exemption covers any building that is fit for living, however he got it. It does not cover a gateway, porch, or balcony.
steps.confusionAlert: The building does not have to be used as a home. It only has to be fit for living, which is why a straw shed or barn still counts.

phrases.english: The verse says: 'a house'
just as a house is fit for living,
so too anything fit for living.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the push of step 30 by limiting the broad reading.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the broad reading by a defining feature (fit for living).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Every structure, even a gateway or balcony, counts.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only a structure fit for living counts, even if he uses it for something else.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב: 'house' means just a house
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב holds that the word 'house' in the פסוק means only an actual house.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב says: 'House' means what it plainly says.
steps.whatsHappening: A different תנא gives his own view. He says the word 'house' should be read plainly, as an actual house.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier part of the ברייתא used the words 'that built' to add straw sheds, barns, wood sheds and storehouses. רבי אליעזר בן יעקב reads 'house' at face value, so those extra buildings do not count. Only a real house exempts a man from battle.

keyTerms.meaning: As it plainly means; read at face value
A תנא who gives his own reading here

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix him up with רבי אליעזר (בן הורקנוס). This is רבי אליעזר בן יעקב, a different תנא.

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer ben Ya'akov says:
"House" means what it plainly says.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a narrower reading than the ברייתא's wider reading in steps 28-31.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only an actual house counts for the exemption of one who built a house.

steps.title: 'Dedicated it' excludes a robber
steps.stepSummary: The extra word 'it' in 'has not dedicated it' teaches that a robber's house does not exempt him.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק could have said 'has not dedicated', but it says 'has not dedicated it'. This excludes a robber.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא reads one more detail in the פסוק. The small word 'it' teaches that a robber does not go home for a house he stole.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Dedicated it' points to a house that truly belongs to the man. A robber's house is not really his, so he is left out of the exemption. This sets up the גמרא's next question.

keyTerms.meaning: Dedicated it; points to a house that is really his

steps.whyThisMatters: This exclusion of the גזלן is the exact point the גמרא questions in the next step.

phrases.english: Not just "has not dedicated," but "and has not dedicated it" —
phrases.notes: דברים 20:5. The extra 'it' means his own house.

phrases.english: this excludes a robber.

steps.triggerLanguage: לֹא חָנַךְ וְלֹא חֲנָכוֹ פְּרָט לְגַזְלָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues reading details of the house פסוק, now about who owns the house.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A robber does not return from battle because of a house he took by robbery.

steps.title: Does excluding the robber disagree with רבי יוסי הגלילי?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that the robber exclusion may not fit רבי יוסי הגלילי, who says 'fainthearted' means someone who is afraid because of his sins.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say this does not follow רבי יוסי הגלילי? Because רבי יוסי הגלילי said that 'and fainthearted' means one who is afraid...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts to challenge the robber rule. It brings רבי יוסי הגלילי's reading of 'fainthearted', and that sentence finishes in the next part of the text.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יוסי הגלילי, the 'fainthearted' man who goes home is someone afraid of his sins. A robber has sins, so it seems he would go home anyway. A special rule leaving him out then seems not to fit רבי יוסי הגלילי's view.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall we say? (opens a suggestion the גמרא tests)
A תנא whose reading of 'fainthearted' is quoted here

steps.confusionAlert: The sentence is not finished yet. 'Afraid' here does not simply mean afraid of battle. The next words explain what he is afraid of.

phrases.english: Shall we say this is not in line with Rabbi Yosei HaGelili?

phrases.aramaic: דְּאִי רַבִּי יוֹסֵי הַגְּלִילִי הָא אָמַר:
phrases.english: For if it were Rabbi Yosei HaGelili, didn't he say:
"And fainthearted" — this is one who is afraid
phrases.notes: דברים 20:8. The sentence continues right after this, explaining what he is afraid of.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the robber rule from step 33 against another תנא's view.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule in step 33 that a robber is left out of the house exemption.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If 'fainthearted' means someone afraid of his sins, a sinner like a robber goes home anyway. So a special rule leaving out the robber seems not to fit רבי יוסי הגלילי.
